newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Monday mainly due to a sharp decrease in fund supply on the market with state banks pulling out of trading, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract surged to 15 percent from 10 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 4.7 million lots from 5.8 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Beijing last week ordered state banks to stop trading on the state debt repo and spot market with immediate effect.
"With the withdrawal of the state banks, money supply has been greatly reduced on the repo market," said one trader. "This made the interest rates for all contracts rise sharply today."
A number of new domestic A share issues scheduled for next few days also helped to boost the repo rates, traders said.
After today's rises, the repo rates are likely to move around the current high levels in the short term, they said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Monday on a technical rebound after heavy losses last Friday, traders said.
But the most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, closed unchanged at 121.20 yuan, indicating market fundamentals had not changed much.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.2 million lots from 1.6 million lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to move narrowly in slow trading in the next few days.
